rubrics.justification: Correctly identifies a low/intermediate-quality blastocyst with loose ICM and scant TE broadly consistent with 2BB, but overstates degeneration/debris and introduces speculative cavitary changes not clearly evident; also shows some confusion around day/stage terminology.

Integrates age, prior IVF history, DOR diagnosis, BMI, endometrium, and semen parameters reasonably well with embryo quality, though AMH is unavailable and some factors (e.g., lifestyle, mild male factor) may be weighted more heavily than evidence supports.

Overall logic is clear and internally consistent: young age and lining improve prognosis while suboptimal morphology and repeated failed cycles reduce it. Minor issues include calling it a day-4 transfer while discussing blastocyst grading and some speculative morphology-based pessimism.

Generally aligned with standard IVF counseling on morphology, prognosis, luteal support, and uterine reassessment after repeated failure, but includes weaker-evidence suggestions (routine sperm DNA fragmentation/chronic endometritis workup, donor oocyte discussion at age 29) and some imprecision regarding Gardner staging/day.

Provides practical next steps for current transfer and contingency planning, including cavity reassessment and cycle review. Recommendations are useful, though some are broad rather than tightly prioritized for this specific case.
